title: United Airlines 2885
summary: A McDonnell Douglas DC-8-54F cargo flight experienced an unstabilized takeoff from Detroit with the horizontal stabilizer incorrectly trimmed to landing configuration instead of takeoff configuration. The crew failed to follow procedural checklists to detect the error. After takeoff, the aircraft climbed to about 1,000 feet with an abnormally steep pitch attitude, then rolled right and descended rapidly into terrain (p. 3-4).
probable_cause: The flightcrew's failure to follow procedural checklist requirements and to detect and correct a mistrimmed stabilizer before the airplane became uncontrollable. Contributing to the accident was the captain's allowing the second officer, who was not qualified to act as a pilot, to occupy the seat of the first officer and to conduct the takeoff (p. 28).

factors.evidence: The horizontal stabilizer trim was at 7.6 units ANU at impact, which was the previous landing trim setting instead of takeoff configuration (p. 28). The flightcrew inadvertently overlooked setting the stabilizer trim for takeoff (p. 28).

The flightcrew failed to follow procedural checklist requirements to detect and correct the mistrimmed stabilizer (p. 28). Had any one of six distinct procedural requirements involving all three crewmembers been followed, the stabilizer landing trim should have been set within acceptable limits at takeoff (p. 28).

The captain allowed the second officer, who was not qualified to act as a pilot, to occupy the seat of the first officer and to conduct the takeoff (p. 3). The second officer had failed to qualify as a DC-8 first officer and subsequently lost the B-737 first officer qualification after a year on the line (p. 28).
The captain and first officer did not have the prescribed crew rest prior to the trip sequence and might have been fatigued (p. 28).

After takeoff, the aircraft's pitch attitude steepened abnormally, and it climbed to about 1,000 feet above ground level. The engines surged during the climb causing visible flames to emit from the engines (p. 28).
After reaching approximately 1,000 feet, the airplane then rolled to the right and descended rapidly to the ground (p. 3).
An explosion and fireball occurred at impact. The airplane was destroyed by impact and by the postimpact fire (p. 3).

events.text: The first officer and second officer swapped duty stations about 6.5 seconds before takeoff with the approval of the captain, with the second officer moving to the first officer seat (p. 28).
Aircraft called for clearance onto runway 21R at 02:49:58 and was cleared for takeoff at 02:50:03 (p. 4).
Takeoff roll was normal and the airplane rotated to takeoff attitude one-half to two-thirds of the way down runway 21R (p. 4).
After liftoff, the airplane's pitch attitude steepened abnormally, and the aircraft began climbing rapidly from the runway surface (p. 4).
The airplane climbed to about 1,000 feet above ground level with the engines surging during the climb, causing visible flames to emit from the engines (p. 28).
After reaching approximately 1,000 feet, the airplane rolled to the right and began descending rapidly to the ground (p. 3).
Aircraft continues rapid descent from approximately 500 feet altitude with increasing right roll (p. 3).

An explosion and fireball occurred as the aircraft impacted terrain. The airplane was destroyed by impact and postimpact fire. The flightcrew, consisting of the captain, the first officer, and the second officer, were killed (p. 3).
